findings.finding: Diversified maker of connectors, cable assemblies, fiber interconnect, antennas and sensors sold to thousands of OEMs, EMS and distributors; no customer is 10% or more of sales; distributors 27.6% of Q3 2026 sales (18.1% a year earlier; the rise is CommScope's channel). No units or ASP: demand is read through orders: Q3 2026 orders a record 12.2B, book-to-bill 1.19 (Q2 1.23, Q1 1.24), orders generally delivered within one year, no RPO.

Q3 2026 sales 10.23B, +65% y/y = 37 points organic + 28 points acquisitions (CommScope CCS closed 2026-01-09 for 10.5B; CommScope FY2026 sales guide raised 4.1B -> 4.6B -> 5.1B). Organic growth re-accelerated: 41%, 41%, 37%, 33%, 30%, 37% (Q2 2025 to Q3 2026). The 10-Q pro forma (CommScope from 2025-01-01) gives 9M 2025 19,368.6M vs reported 16,655.7M: CommScope's pre-deal size about 2.7B for nine months (about 3.6B a year). FY2027 growth is almost all organic; small deals (Empire about 320M a year, closed September; AdvancedPCB, Humanetics, Dexgreen pending, 1.6B combined price) add a little.

IT datacom went from 36% of FY2025 sales to 43% of Q2 2026 with +63% organic, virtually all AI-related per management; Communications Solutions (the segment holding datacom and CommScope) grew 51% organic in Q3 against 29% Harsh Environment and 11% Interconnect and Sensor. Roughly half of organic growth is the hyperscaler AI wave (cyclical in amplitude), the rest broad-based (defense, air, industrial). Q3 end-market split not read (transcript gap).

End customers' own capex and production (hyperscalers and their ODMs for AI racks, defense budgets, industrial and auto OEMs); no vendor financing, take-or-pay or multi-year contracted volume disclosed. Visibility is two to three quarters through short-dated orders. Purchase commitments 2.0B due 2026 vs 72M 2027-2028.

GAAP operating margin 29.5% in Q3 2026 (3,020.8 / 10,229.7; adjusted 29.7%, tariff recovery only 15M) and 29.5% in Q2, against 19.1-20.7% in FY2020-FY2024 and 25.4% in FY2025; TTM 27.7% (9.16B / 33.05B). Incremental operating margin about 33% on 65% growth. Part structural mix (AI datacom), part peak operating leverage of a growth wave: the base mature margin sits between FY2025 and TTM, not at the Q3 run rate.

Revenue guide midpoint beaten 8 of 8 recorded quarters (7 in auto.json to Q2 plus Q3 2026: 10.23B vs 9.35B midpoint, ratio 1.094); mean ratio 1.11, lowest 1.064. A conservative guider: the first fiscal-year guide 36.9-37.1B (Q4 10.3-10.5B, about +60%) is a floor. Part of the early beats came from an accelerating cycle and acquisitions.

Q3 normalised net income 2.10B vs reported 2.03B (tariff recovery removed, 15.5M deal costs and 60M discrete foreign tax items added back, symmetric). SBC small (47M, 0.5% of sales) and already in GAAP. Q3 FCF 1.62B = 80% of net income; 9M capex 1.10B = 4.2% of sales (top of the 3-4% guide); working capital absorbed 416M in Q3 (DSO 70 days, DIO 78 days) as sales grow.

findings.topic: forensic screens, returns and the CommScope price
findings.finding: Piotroski 7 of 8 (strong; miss = new shares), Altman Z'' 5.0 (safe); Beneish and ROIC unavailable from the screen. CommScope earned 471.4M before interest and deal costs on 3.68B of sales from close to 2026-09-30 (about 6% a year on the 10.5B price, after purchase accounting): below the cost of capital so far, though its guide keeps rising (accretion 0.075 -> 0.15 -> 0.18 per share).

Debt 17.87B, cash and short-term investments 5.30B, net debt 12.57B at 2026-09-30 (from about 2B net cash pre-CommScope); goodwill 17.70B is above equity 17.12B. Interest expense 212.3M a quarter (80.7M a year earlier). Buybacks 245M and dividends 308M in Q3; dividend raised to 0.15 from 2027-01; diluted shares +0.7% y/y (buybacks cover SBC).

China 14.1% of Q3 2026 sales (1,441.1 of 10,229.7) and 37% of long-lived assets at 2025-12-31; US 38.8%. China tax inquiries cost 100M (Q4 2025) + 290M (H1 2026) and 60M of discrete foreign tax items in Q3: an unresolved, unsized residual.

flags: operating margin 29.5% far above the 2020-2024 range (19-21%): peak-cycle earnings power until proven otherwise (carried to bear and key risk)
acquisition-driven growth: 28 of 65 points in Q3 2026 bought; CommScope returns about 6% a year on its 10.5B price so far
goodwill 17.7B above stockholders' equity 17.1B; net debt 12.6B after CommScope
Piotroski miss: new shares issued (diluted shares +0.7% y/y)
concentration in the hyperscaler AI capex cycle: IT datacom 43% of sales (Q2 2026), virtually all of its growth AI
China: 14% of sales, 37% of long-lived assets, recurring tax-inquiry charges (100M + 290M + 60M discrete)
Beneish and ROIC not computed by the screen (inputs missing)

economics.reason: Seven end markets, no 10% customer; revenue fell only once in 2020-2025 (FY2023 -0.5% after +16%) with operating margin held 19-21% through it. A cycle treatment would revert the acquired CommScope revenue to an old trend. The AI-capex cyclicality is handled explicitly: base margin below the run rate and an AI-pause bear.
